cultural_context.description: Andhra Pradesh has a diverse cultural heritage expressed through Telugu language and literature, classical and folk arts, temple traditions, festivals, crafts, cuisine, textiles, and regional traditions across coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
cultural_context.important_note: Cultural practices vary across regions, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in Andhra Pradesh.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation
source.title: Andhra Pradesh Tourism

communication_guidance: Use respectful communication when interacting with local people.
Andhra Pradesh has linguistic, regional, religious, and community diversity, so do not assume one communication style represents everyone.
When participating in a cultural or religious event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or the relevant venue.
greetings_and_communication.limitation: The current verified knowledge base does not contain a sufficiently sourced everyday Telugu phrase list. Do not invent Telugu phrases or translations.

verified_information.description: Andhra Pradesh Tourism documents Andhra cuisine as an important part of the state's cultural identity, with regional food traditions and distinctive preparations.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism
source.title: Cuisine

verified_information.description: Food traditions vary across different parts of Andhra Pradesh, including coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, so one style should not be treated as representative of the entire state.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism
source.title: Andhra Pradesh Tourism

dining_guidance: Do not assume one Andhra dish or food tradition represents the entire state.
Food practices can vary according to region, religion, community, family tradition, and individual preference.
Respect individual dietary choices and follow local hosts' guidance at traditional meals and community events.
food_and_dining.limitation: The verified knowledge base does not establish universal everyday dining etiquette for every region and community in Andhra Pradesh.

core_values.name: Regional cultural diversity
core_values.description: Andhra Pradesh contains distinct regional traditions, including cultural differences between coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism
source.title: Andhra Pradesh Tourism

core_values.name: Living artistic traditions
core_values.description: Classical dance, folk performance, crafts, textiles, temple traditions, and festivals form important parts of Andhra Pradesh's documented cultural heritage.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

festivals.name: Ugadi
festivals.description: Ugadi is celebrated as the Telugu New Year and is an important traditional festival in Andhra Pradesh.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

festivals.name: Sankranti
festivals.description: Sankranti is a major harvest festival in Andhra Pradesh and is associated with seasonal, agricultural, family, and community traditions.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

festivals.name: Tirumala Brahmotsavam
festivals.description: Brahmotsavam is a major religious festival associated with the Tirumala temple tradition and attracts large numbers of devotees.

source.organization: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams
source.title: Srivari Brahmotsavam

festivals.name: Lepakshi Festival
festivals.description: The Lepakshi Festival is associated with the heritage setting of Lepakshi and presents cultural performances and local traditions.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism
source.title: Andhra Pradesh Tourism

festivals.name: Dasara
festivals.description: Dasara is celebrated in Andhra Pradesh with regional and religious variations.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

traditional_dances.name: Kuchipudi
traditional_dances.description: Kuchipudi is a major Indian classical dance tradition originating in Andhra Pradesh. It combines dance, expressive storytelling, music, and theatrical elements.

source.organization: Ministry of Culture, Government of India
source.title: Kuchipudi

traditional_dances.name: Dhimsa
traditional_dances.description: Dhimsa is a tribal folk dance tradition associated with tribal communities of the northern Andhra Pradesh region and is performed in community and festival contexts.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

traditional_dances.name: Kolattam
traditional_dances.description: Kolattam is a traditional group folk dance using sticks and is documented among Andhra Pradesh's folk traditions.

source.organization: Andhra Pradesh Tourism
source.title: Andhra Pradesh Tourism

traditional_clothing.name: Traditional Andhra attire
traditional_clothing.description: Traditional clothing forms part of Andhra Pradesh's cultural and festival life. Sarees, dhotis, and regionally distinctive textiles are associated with traditional dress, but clothing varies by region, community, religion, occasion, and individual preference.

source.organization: Ministry of Tourism, Government of India
source.title: Andhra Pradesh

traditional_clothing.name: Mangalagiri textiles
traditional_clothing.description: Mangalagiri is documented for its handloom textile tradition, including distinctive cotton fabrics and sarees.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Mangalagiri Sarees and Fabrics

traditional_arts.name: Kalamkari
traditional_arts.description: Kalamkari is a traditional textile and painting craft associated with Andhra Pradesh, using hand-drawn or block-printed designs on cloth.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Kalamkari

traditional_arts.name: Kondapalli toys
traditional_arts.description: Kondapalli wooden toys are a traditional craft associated with Kondapalli in Andhra Pradesh and are made from locally sourced lightweight wood.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Kondapalli Toys

traditional_arts.name: Etikoppaka toys
traditional_arts.description: Etikoppaka is known for traditional lacquered wooden toys and craft products made using a distinctive lac-turnery technique.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Etikoppaka Toys

traditional_arts.name: Uppada handloom
traditional_arts.description: Uppada is associated with a handloom weaving tradition in Andhra Pradesh, particularly known for sarees and fine weaving.

source.organization: Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
source.title: Uppada Sarees

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Temple traditions
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Andhra Pradesh has major temple traditions and pilgrimage centers, including Tirumala, where religious observances and festivals are important parts of cultural life.

source.title: Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Sankranti cultural traditions

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Folk traditions such as Dhimsa represent particular tribal communities and should be described in their local context rather than generalized to all residents of Andhra Pradesh.

visitor_guidance: Treat temples, religious ceremonies, festivals, folk performances, and community celebrations with respect.
When entering temples or other sacred spaces, follow the venue's instructions regarding clothing, footwear, photography, and behavior.
Ask before photographing people, ritual performers, religious ceremonies, or culturally significant activities when permission or local rules are unclear.
Do not assume that a practice associated with coastal Andhra or Rayalaseema applies to the entire state.
Do not generalize tribal or community-specific traditions such as Dhimsa to all residents of Andhra Pradesh.
Do not treat religious or ritual practices simply as entertainment.
Respect local hosts and organizers when participating in festivals or cultural events.
